findings.claim: GET/POST /api/v1/accounts/:account_id/conversations/:conversation_id/labels maps index/create. LabelsController uses @conversation and permits conversation_id plus labels: [] (array); it does not establish a label-title whitelist.
findings.critical_dependency: A-Q1, answered B-A1; source independently inspected.

findings.claim: POST assigns label_list through update_labels/update!; distinct add_labels combines labels. GET reads label_list; POST reads it after update. Both responses use {payload: labels}.
Lookup is account-associated display_id, followed by show? authorization. Account label CRUD instead operates Current.account.labels with label title/description/color/show_on_sidebar fields.
Existing POST success assertions check new label substrings; they do not assert old labels removed or exact payload. Proposed replacement/payload regression check remains unverified.

dependency_messages.question_or_answer: Is the conversation lookup account scoped and based on display_id, and what access evidence exists?

SOURCE_OBSERVED: POST create calls model.update_labels(permitted_params[:labels]) then reads model.label_list. update_labels uses update!(label_list: labels), an assignment; it does not call distinct add_labels, whose implementation combines existing/new labels. Both create/index templates use json.payload @labels, so response has a payload wrapper. Exact persistence normalization/callback behavior is outside manifest and NOT_RUN.

Accounts::BaseController lines 5-7 invokes current_account and conditionally API-access/MFA guards.
